messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 52-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3.6-kg (8-lb) weight loss over the past 3 months and increasing fatigue. He was diagnosed with hepatitis C 6 years ago. His father died of colon cancer. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years and drinks one beer daily. He used cocaine and heroin in the past but stopped 12 years ago. He is 176 cm (5 ft 8 in) tall and weighs 71 kg (156 lb); BMI is 22.9 kg/m2. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 79/min, and blood pressure is 115/75 mm Hg. He appears weak and lethargic. Examination shows scleral icterus and scars on both cubital fossae. There is reddening of the palms bilaterally. There are several telangiectasias over the chest and back. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The liver is firm and of nodular consistency. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 11.6 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3
Leukocyte count 9,600/mm3
Platelet count 223,000/mm3
Ultrasonography of the liver shows a solitary lesion. Which of the following findings is most likely in this patient?"

Options:
A. Positive blood cultures
B. Elevated α-fetoprotein
C. Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen
D. Exophytic tumor on colonoscopy
E. Spiculated lesion on chest CT

Correct answer: B. Elevated α-fetoprotein

text: {"psychiatry": false, "dsm_answerable": false, "category": "other", "reason": "This is a hepatology/oncology question about hepatocellular carcinoma in a cirrhotic patient; the remote substance use history is incidental and DSM-5 knowledge is irrelevant."}
